html:
SMTO-TSK-0046 — This step was stopped before it started

GUID: e55ad037-b923-47f1-921f-7fd095beeb6f
Slug: activity-stopped
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • This step was waiting for a free slot when the task was stopped, so SMTO cancelled it before it began. The step never ran, so nothing it would have done has happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the task in the conversation and confirm it shows as stopped, or that you selected Stop on it or on this step. This message only appears when a stop arrived while the step was still waiting its turn.
  2. If you still want the work done, send a new message in the conversation asking for it. The stopped step never ran, so asking again starts it fresh instead of repeating something that already happened.

What success looks like

  • The step is shown as cancelled and not started, and any new request you send runs normally.

If it still fails

  • If steps keep being cancelled when you did not select Stop, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the same request in a loop; check why it is being stopped first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The activity worker cancelled a non-dependency activity before execution because the task was stopped while the activity waited for background capacity (background.capacity returned False after a stop was recorded).

What this means

  • Background-capacity admission returns false for an eligible non-dependency activity, causing an interrupted admission and unexecuted cancelled activity state. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • Background-capacity admission returns false for an eligible non-dependency activity, causing an interrupted admission and unexecuted cancelled activity state.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect background admission and stop state; the label alone does not prove the user explicitly stopped this activity.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • Treat this as an expected cancellation, not a failure: the activity is recorded as cancelled with executed=false. Confirm in the task's activity list or event log that a run-level Stop or an activity_stop event was recorded; if the work is still wanted, request it as new work rather than replaying this activity.

Retry and execution caution

  • This state requests no new execution or automatic retry. Inspect the current task controls and retained results.

How to verify the fix

  • The original activity is settled as unstarted and later work follows current admission controls.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
